CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows an N–H stretching band at 3342 cm⁻¹, so the molecule must contain at least one ­NH bond; most candidates are fully N-alkylated and lack N–H, but candidate 3 (dimethylamine, CN(C)N) has a single N–H.  The very strong C–H stretches at 2949, 2870 and 2845 cm⁻¹ fit the two methyl groups of dimethylamine, while the intense 738 cm⁻¹ band matches the characteristic CH₃ rocking vibration (∼730–760 cm⁻¹) of dimethyl-substituted amines.  Bands at 1458 and 1411 cm⁻¹ correspond to CH₃ bending modes (δ_as and δ_s), 1601 cm⁻¹ to the NH bend (ρ(NH) ~1600 cm⁻¹ in secondary amines), and 1149 cm⁻¹ to the C–N stretch (ν(C–N) 1020–1250 cm⁻¹).  No other candidate simultaneously provides an N–H bond and the simple alkyl vibrational pattern seen here.
